articles.title: Ex matou jovem para evitar que atual descobrisse reaproximação, diz MP | G1
articles.standfirst: Jovem de 18 anos atraiu Ana Rerica de Messias, de 19 anos, para um local ermo e a atacou após uma discussão, segundo as investigações da polícia. Ele virou réu.
articles.summary: A Justiça aceitou a denúncia contra o ex-namorado de Ana Rerica de Messias, acusado de cometer o feminicídio em Morrinhos para ocultar a reaproximação da atual companheira.
articles.body:
A Justiça do Ceará aceitou a denúncia do Ministério Público do Ceará (MPCE) contra Francisco Dionatas Mota de Sousa, acusado de matar a facadas a ex-namorada, a universitária Ana Rerica de Messias, de 19 anos . Dionatas vai responder pelo crime de feminicídio. Segundo a denúncia do MP, ele matou a jovem para evitar que sua atual namorada descobrisse a reaproximação dos dois.

O crime aconteceu na noite do dia 29 de maio em uma estrada carroçável da localidade de Bom Princípio, no município de Morrinhos , a cerca de 210 quilômetros de Fortaleza. Conforme o inquérito policial, Ana Rérica foi morta com vários golpes de uma faca de cozinha.

Ana Rérica e Dionatas haviam tido um breve relacionamento cerca de quatro anos antes do crime. Os dois se conheciam desde a adolescência e o jovem dançou a valsa com ela na festa de aniversário de 15 anos de Rérica.

Nos últimos meses, eles voltaram a ter contato, ensaiando uma possível aproximação. Segundo a denúncia do Ministério Público, à qual o g1 teve acesso, para se reaproximar da jovem, Dionatas teria dito que havia terminado o atual relacionamento e estava solteiro.

No dia 26 de maio, três dias antes do crime, eles haviam se encontrado, e o suspeito marcou um novo encontro para o dia 29, noite do crime. Segundo a Polícia Civil, Dionatas atacou Rérica após uma discussão. Conforme o MP, ele teria matado Ana Rérica na tentativa de evitar que sua atual namorada descobrisse a reaproximação.

Homem de 18 anos foi preso por suspeita de matar a universitária Ana Rerica de Messias, de 19 anos, na cidade de Morrinhos, no Ceará. — Foto: Reprodução

Ainda segundo o MP, "durante as investigações, ficou evidenciado que o relacionamento dos dois era abusivo e que o denunciado mantinha controle emocional e psicológico sobre a jovem". Ele foi denunciado pelo crime de feminicídio qualificado por uso de meio cruel e sem possibilidade de defesa da vítima.

A denúncia do MP foi apresentada à Justiça no início de agosto e aceita pela juízo da Comarca de Marco cinco dias depois. Francisco Dionatas está em prisão preventiva desde o dia 23 de junho, após ser detido no município de Bela Cruz , a cerca de 23 quilômetros de Morrinhos, onde o crime ocorreu.

No mesmo dia da prisão de Francisco Dionatas, a casa onde ele vivia foi incendiada e e atingida por tiros de arma de fogo. As chamas destruíram um carro que estava estacionado no alpendre e se espalharam pelo imóvel.

Univesitária Ana Rerica de Messias, de 19 anos, foi encontrada morta em via pública na cidade de Morrinhos, no interior do Ceará. — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Familiares descreveram Ana Rerica como muito querida e bastante esforçada. Além de trabalhar em uma escola, ela também estudava e frequentava a igreja.

O irmão da jovem, André Messias, de 21 anos, disse ao g1 que Ana Rerica tinha uma rotina dividida entre trabalho, igreja e amigos. Pela manhã, ela atuava como Profissional de Apoio a Crianças com Necessidades Especiais na rede municipal de ensino.

No início da tarde, a jovem dava aulas de reforço e entre o fim da tarde e o início da noite ajudava em uma loja de uma tia. Ela frequentava a igreja Assembleia de Deus Bela Vista e cursava uma graduação em Pedagogia online.

Ana Rerica foi encontrada morta em via pública na noite de sexta-feira (30) — Foto: Reprodução

No tempo livre, ela gostava de visitar os amigos e andar de moto na cidade de pouco mais de 20 mil habitantes. Além disso, a universitária era muito querida no trabalho pois se dava bem com crianças -- inclusive, já tinha feito alguns bicos como babá para conhecidos.

"Sempre trabalhou com crianças, sempre se deu bem com criança porque no fundo ainda era uma criança", disse André Messias. "Por isso toda criança que ela trabalhava gostava dela."

A morte de Ana Rérica gerou comoção na cidade. O velório ocorreu no dia 30 de maio, na igreja que ela frequentava. Antes da jovem ser enterrada, foi feito o cortejo fúnebre da igreja para o cemitério. O momento foi acompanhado por dezenas de pessoas, alguns com cartazes que pediam justiça pela universitária.

articles.title: Colapso de geleira pode ter desencadeado a avalanche mortal no Nepal | G1
articles.standfirst: Ainda não está claro, contudo, o que causou o colapso da geleira. As causas ainda estão sendo investigadas.
articles.summary: Não ficou claro, contudo, o que causou o colapso da geleira. As causas ainda estão sendo investigadas.
articles.body:
Uma enchente repentina e mortal ocorrida nesta quarta-feira perto da fronteira do Nepal com o Tibete pode ter sido provocada pelo desprendimento da parte inferior de uma geleira , que desabou no fundo do vale, centenas de metros abaixo, afirmam especialistas, com base em imagens de satélite da Planet Labs.

Não ficou claro, contudo, o que causou o colapso da geleira. As causas ainda estão sendo investigadas.

➡️ O desastre deixou ao menos 160 mortos e centenas de desaparecidos nos dois lados da fronteira .

Imagens de satélite da região antes e depois, fornecidas pela Planet Labs e vistas pela Reuters , mostraram a encosta verdejante agora soterrada sob detritos e sedimentos marrons.

“Está confirmado que uma parte substancial da ponta da geleira desabou, desencadeando o evento — provavelmente incluindo ou arrastando uma quantidade considerável de rochas e sedimentos”, disse Vikram Gupta, especialista em geologia de engenharia e professor da Universidade de Sikkim, na Índia.

O cientista da Terra Dan Shugar, professor associado da Universidade de Calgary, disse que as imagens parecem indicar que uma grande quantidade de neve derreteu nas 24 horas anteriores ao desastre.

Uma combinação de imagens de satélite mostra os vales perto da fronteira entre o Nepal e a China em 25 de agosto de 2026, antes das inundações devastadoras (T), e em 26 de agosto de 2026, após o desastre (B). — Foto: Reuters

“Algumas das geleiras do vale estavam cobertas de neve ontem e hoje estão, em sua maioria, com o gelo à mostra. Portanto, em outras palavras (e ainda não vi nenhum dado de estações meteorológicas), provavelmente estava quente”, disse ele.

As montanhas cobertas de neve do Nepal perderam quase um terço de seu gelo em pouco mais de 30 anos devido ao aquecimento global, informou a Organização das Nações Unidas em 2023. A agência acrescentou naquele ano que as geleiras do Nepal, situadas entre dois grandes emissores de carbono — Índia e China —, derreteram 65% mais rápido na última década do que na anterior .

“Pelo que posso ver nas imagens de satélite desta manhã da Planet Labs, a parte inferior de uma geleira se desprendeu a cerca de 5.200 metros e desabou no fundo do vale, cerca de 1.200 metros abaixo”, disse Shugar.

Ele afirmou que as obras também podem ter sido um fator e que “se as mudanças climáticas tiveram algum papel nisso, é algo que, sem dúvida, investigaremos em um futuro próximo”.

GIF - destruição na fronteira do Nepal com o Tibete — Foto: Reprodução/ g1

Vários projetos hidrelétricos estão localizados nas áreas mais afetadas no distrito montanhoso de Rasuwa, que tem uma população de cerca de 50 mil habitantes.

A Agência Nacional de Redução e Gestão de Riscos de Desastres do Nepal informou que a “inundação com geleira” ocorreu no rio Lhende devido a um deslizamento de terra que aconteceu a cerca de 20 km a nordeste de um posto de fronteira entre o Nepal e a China.

Relatos iniciais apontaram diferentes possibilidades para a origem da avalanche e das enchentes, mas Prakash Pokharel, geólogo da agência, disse que ainda não está claro o que provocou a tragédia.

“As enchentes repentinas foram causadas por uma avalanche de gelo e rochas no lado nepalês”, disse Pokharel, que analisou as imagens da Planet Labs.

Inundações, deslizamentos de terra, avalanches e secas estão aumentando em frequência e intensidade em todo o Hindu Kush-Himalaia, e as mudanças aceleradas na água, no solo e no ar em toda a região representam uma grande ameaça para as pessoas, afirma o Centro Internacional para o Desenvolvimento Integrado das Montanhas.

O grupo informou nesta quarta-feira que a enchente repentina provocou uma forte onda de água, sedimentos e pedras pelos sistemas fluviais dos rios Bhote Koshi e Trishuli, acrescentando que os níveis de água no rio na área de Galchhi, a jusante, teriam subido até nove metros em 30 minutos.

Imagem tirada de dentro de um carro mostrando propriedades cobertas de lama após uma enchente repentina em Trishuli, no distrito de Nuwakot, no Nepal 26 de agosto de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Navesh Chitrakar

articles.title: O que muda nas redes nos EUA após acordo bilionário da Meta | G1
articles.standfirst: Acordo encerra ações movidas por 47 estados americanos e prevê limite diário de uso, bloqueio noturno, verificação de idade e controles parentais mais rígidos no Facebook e Instagram.
articles.summary: Acordo encerra ações movidas por 47 estados americanos e prevê limite diário de uso, bloqueio noturno, verificação de idade e controles parentais mais rígidos.
articles.body:
Adam Mosseri, chefe do Instagram, deixa o Tribunal após julgamento em que a Meta está sendo processada por 'incentivar' vício de adolescentes nas redes sociais. — Foto: KARL MONDON/AFP

A Meta fechou um acordo no qual aceitou pagar em torno de US$ 17 bilhões (R$ 87,7 bilhões) e adicionar medidas de segurança mais robustas para proteger as crianças em suas plataformas Facebook e Instagram.

A decisão encerra um julgamento histórico nos Estados Unidos sobre o vício em redes sociais entre adolescentes e resolve as ações movidas por 47 dos 50 estados americanos , anunciaram na quarta-feira (26) os procuradores-gerais estaduais.

O caso buscava responsabilizar a gigante da tecnologia pelo papel que suas plataformas desempenharam na deterioração da saúde mental das crianças.

A Meta foi acusada de contribuir para a crise de saúde mental juvenil ao projetar deliberadamente recursos que viciam crianças em suas plataformas e escondê-los do público.

Os reclamantes também argumentaram que a empresa violou leis federais ao coletar rotineiramente dados de crianças menores de 13 anos sem o consentimento dos pais

O acordo selado nesta quarta-feira deve encerrar o processo judicial envolvendo os estados da Califórnia, Colorado, Kentucky e Nova Jersey, que estavam entre os 29 que processaram a Meta em 2023.

O CEO da empresa, Mark Zuckerberg , estava entre os que deveriam depor perante um júri em um tribunal federal na Califórnia.

Os casos em outros estados devem ir a julgamento posteriormente. Além disso, nove procuradores-gerais entraram com ações judiciais em seus respectivos estados.

O julgamento começou na semana passada em Oakland, Califórnia, com a juíza distrital dos EUA, Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers, supervisionando os procedimentos. A Meta estimou o valor do acordo em cerca de US$ 18 bilhões, número que aparentemente inclui uma indenização para o estado do Texas.

Acordo "encerra práticas perigosas" da Meta

"Durante anos, a Meta enganou intencionalmente o público sobre os recursos de design viciantes e prejudiciais que causaram estragos na saúde mental dos jovens", disse o procurador-geral da Virgínia, Jay Jones.

O acordo, segundo ele, " colocará um fim a essas práticas perigosas e proporcionará um alívio significativo que protegerá as crianças de danos online ".

O procurador-geral da Califórnia, Rob Bonta, disse que o dinheiro será pago ao longo de dez anos, com seu estado recebendo pelo menos US$ 1,5 bilhão se o acordo for aprovado pelo tribunal. Nova Jersey espera receber pelo menos US$ 525 milhões , enquanto Massachusetts poderá receber pelo menos US$ 366 milhões . A parte que cabe à Virgínia é de US$ 353 milhões .

A Meta afirmou em uma postagem que estava "dando continuidade aos nossos esforços de longa data para capacitar pais e apoiar adolescentes".

"Garantir que os adolescentes tenham uma experiência segura e produtiva em nossas plataformas é um imperativo absoluto para a Meta", disse a empresa. " Queremos acertar isso junto a pais e adolescentes, e é por isso que firmamos parceria com procuradores-gerais estaduais para estabelecer um novo padrão do setor. "

A empresa incentivou seus concorrentes, TikTok e YouTube , a adotarem medidas de segurança semelhantes.

O acordo de US$ 17 bilhões representa uma fração da receita da Meta em 2025, de US$ 201 bilhões.

Nos termos do acordo proposto, a Meta concordou em adotar uma série de recursos de segurança, incluindo limites diários de tempo de uso e pausas obrigatórias para crianças que usam o Instagram e o Facebook.

A empresa eliminará as notificações push durante o horário escolar em dias de semana e implementará medidas robustas de verificação de idade e controles de conteúdo apropriados para cada faixa etária, a fim de prevenir o bullying e a disseminação de material prejudicial sobre temas como distúrbios alimentares e automutilação .

As notificações push também deverão ser desativadas entre as 22h e as 7h.

Haverá controles parentais mais fortes e fáceis de usar, além de limites para recursos de comparação social, como a contagem de curtidas. Um auditor independente avaliará como a Meta está implementando os recursos de segurança e qual a sua eficácia.

A Meta deverá pagar o valor estipulado em dez parcelas anuais , totalizando cerca de US$ 11,7 bilhões, com outros US$ 5,3 bilhões a serem pagos aos estados somente se plataformas concorrentes assinarem acordos semelhantes. Isso atingiria um máximo de US$ 16,7 bilhões.

Separadamente, a empresa pagaria US$ 75 milhões para cobrir os custos legais dos estados e US$ 459 milhões para resolver antigas reivindicações relacionadas ao escândalo de dados da Cambridge Analytica – caso de uso indevido de dados pessoais de milhões de usuários do Facebook para influenciar eleições e veicular propaganda política, revelado em 2018.

No entanto, a empresa afirmou que 30% do valor total – cerca de US$ 5,3 bilhões – só serão liberados para os estados se as concorrentes YouTube e TikTok cumprirem duas condições: implementar recursos de segurança semelhantes, incluindo um limite diário de uma hora, um bloqueio noturno e medidas de verificação de idade ; e pagar valor equivalente, dividido entre as duas empresas.

A Alphabet , proprietária do Google e do YouTube, e o TikTok não se pronunciaram imediatamente sobre o acordo desta quarta-feira.

Espera-se que os estados gastem o dinheiro em programas de saúde mental para jovens, linhas de apoio em crises, atividades extracurriculares e alfabetização digital, embora as decisões finais caibam às assembleias legislativas estaduais.

Dentro de seis meses, os perfis de adolescentes deverão ser bloqueados no Facebook e no Instagram da meia-noite às 6h. As mensagens e as configurações permaneceriam disponíveis, mas com recursos limitados para que os jovens não possam usá-las para acessar o restante do aplicativo.

As contas teriam um limite padrão de duas horas de uso diário cumulativo nos aplicativos da Meta, reiniciando à meia-noite. Mensagens e vídeos longos não contam para o total. O toque de recolher e o limite não podem ser alterados por um adolescente sem a aprovação dos pais.

Se plataformas concorrentes adotarem compromissos equivalentes, o bloqueio noturno se estenderá das 22h às 7h e o limite diário cairá para 60 minutos por aplicativo, com um máximo de duas horas no total.

Dentro de quatro meses, os adolescentes deverão ter acesso a um feed que não é personalizado por algoritmos. A contagem de curtidas seria ocultada e os filtros de cirurgia plástica seriam bloqueados.

A Meta tem um ano para implementar um sistema preciso de verificação de idade. As ferramentas de verificação não devem identificar erroneamente mais de 3% dos jovens de 13 a 15 anos como adultos, e não mais de 10% dos jovens de 16 e 17 anos.

Novos perfis cuja idade não for verificada após 14 dias serão tratados como contas de adolescentes, independentemente da idade declarada.

Para usuários menores de 13 anos, que são proibidos de usar as plataformas de acordo com a legislação dos EUA, a Meta deve presumir que uma conta denunciada é de menor de idade, a menos que haja evidências em contrário, além de verificar as redes de amigos de contas excluídas em busca de outros usuários menores de idade.

Os pais que supervisionam uma conta de adolescente receberão notificações diárias sobre o tempo gasto, lembretes para revisar as configurações e a possibilidade de ajustar o horário escolar.

A Meta deve responder às denúncias de conteúdo ilegal ou ofensivo feitas por adolescentes em até seis horas em pelo menos 90% dos casos registrados em inglês ou espanhol.

Um auditor independente, escolhido em conjunto pela Meta e por um comitê de estados e pago pela empresa, deverá monitorar o cumprimento do acordo geral durante dez anos.

Uma decisão separada impede a Meta de fazer declarações falsas ou enganosas sobre seus recursos de segurança.

articles.title: Preguiça é resgatada às margens de estrada em Itaperuna | G1
articles.standfirst: Animal foi encontrado na região de Retiro do Muriaé e passou por avaliação veterinária antes de ser solto no Refúgio de Vida Silvestre, na região de Raposo.
articles.summary: Fêmea foi encontrada na região de Retiro do Muriaé e passou por avaliação veterinária antes de ser solta no Refúgio de Vida Silvestre, na região de Raposo.
articles.body:
Uma preguiça foi resgatada nesta quarta-feira (26) em Itaperuna , no Norte Fluminense, após ser encontrada por um casal às margens de uma estrada, na região de Retiro do Muriaé, distrito do município.

Segundo a Guarda Ambiental, o casal levou o animal para a varanda de uma residência e acionou a Secretaria Municipal de Meio Ambiente.

Uma equipe foi até o imóvel e resgatou a preguiça. O médico-veterinário realizou uma avaliação clínica e constatou que o animal, uma fêmea, estava com saúde e em condições de retornar à natureza.

Preguiça resgatada estava em boas condições de saúde e foi solta na natureza — Foto: Secretaria de Meio Ambiente de Itaperuna

Segundo o médico-veterinário Wellington Costa o animal é uma preguiça-comum, da espécie Bradypus variegatus .

"Ela é conhecida como preguiça-de-garganta-marrom, típica aqui da região", disse.

Após a avaliação, a preguiça foi levada para uma área protegida e solta no Refúgio de Vida Silvestre (REVIS), na região de Raposo, em Itaperuna.

Animal foi solto em área de preservação ambiental na região de Raposo, em Itaperuna. — Foto: Secretaria de Meio Ambiente de Itaperuna

articles.title: As imagens de satélite do Nepal que mostram o antes e depois das áreas destruídas pela enxurrada | G1
articles.standfirst: Mais de 150 pessoas morreram e centenas de turistas estão desaparecidos na tragédia.
articles.summary: Mais de 150 pessoas morreram e centenas de turistas estão desaparecidos na tragédia.
articles.body:
Imagens de satélite de antes e depois mostram as inundações nas áreas ao redor do rio Trishuli, na fronteira entre o Nepal e o Tibete.

São duas composições. A primeira imagem de cada uma foi feita há três dias, antes da inundação repentina, enquanto a segunda, registrada nesta quarta-feira (26/8), mostra o rio com o nível elevado e água nas áreas do entorno.

Uma grande enxurrada repentina e um deslizamento de terra causaram destruição na fronteira entre o Nepal e o Tibete nesta quarta-feira (26/8).

As causas da tragédia ainda estão sendo apuradas. Uma análise indica até o momento que um deslizamento de terra precedeu a inundação repentina no Nepal e que não houve um terremoto, informou o Serviço Geológico dos Estados Unidos (USGS).

Mais de 150 pessoas morreram e centenas de turistas estão desaparecidos do lado nepalês. Entre os desaparecidos, estão quase 579 viajantes, sendo 466 estrangeiros e 61 nepaleses, segundo a atualização mais recente do Conselho de Turismo do Nepal.

Os estrangeiros são de 28 países diferentes. Há 133 desaparecidos da Índia, 54 dos Estados Unidos e 33 do Reino Unido.

No lado tibetano, o deslizamento deixou ao menos três mortos e 265 desaparecidos, segundo a emissora estatal chinesa CCTV. O balanço foi divulgado às 20h do horário local.

A maioria seguia rumo ao Kailash Mansarovar, no Tibete. A rota afetada também dá acesso ao Parque Nacional de Langtang e ao lago sagrado de Gosainkunda.

O Itamaraty afirmou que, até o momento, não há informações sobre brasileiros desaparecidos.

articles.title: SP amplia cobertura vacinal contra sarampo e mantém campanha nos 645 municípios até 1º de setembro | G1
articles.standfirst: Estado ficou acima da média nacional nas duas doses da tríplice viral de 2023 a 2025; Dia D aplicou mais de 600 mil doses de diferentes vacinas.
articles.summary: Estado ficou acima da média nacional nas duas doses da tríplice viral de 2023 a 2025; Dia D aplicou mais de 600 mil doses de diferentes vacinas.
articles.body:
Surto de sarampo leva São Paulo e cidades da Grande SP a ampliar vacinação contra a doença — Foto: TV Globo / Reprodução

O estado de São Paulo manterá até 1º de setembro duas frentes de mobilização para ampliar a vacinação: uma multivacinal, para todos os municípios, com foco na atualização das cadernetas de crianças e adolescentes, e outra com foco na imunização contra o sarampo na capital, em Guarulhos e São Bernardo do Campo.

Segundo a Secretaria Estadual da Saúde, a Campanha de Multivacinação vai seguir nos 645 municípios para atualizar a caderneta de crianças e adolescentes menores de 15 anos. Na capital, em Guarulhos e em São Bernardo do Campo, pessoas de 6 meses a 59 anos também podem receber a vacina contra o sarampo, independentemente do histórico vacinal.

No Dia D, realizado no último sábado (22), segundo dados preliminares do Centro de Vigilância Epidemiológica do Estado de São Paulo (CVE-SP), foram aplicadas mais de 600 mil doses de diferentes vacinas em todo o estado.

A mobilização dá continuidade às ações adotadas para recuperar as coberturas vacinais. Entre 2023 e 2025, São Paulo ficou acima da média nacional nas duas doses da tríplice viral, que protege contra sarampo, caxumba e rubéola.

A cobertura da primeira dose no estado passou de 78,4%, em 2022, para 90,8%, em 2023, e chegou a 99,4% em 2024. Em 2025, ficou em 94,2%. Na segunda dose, o índice avançou de 65,1%, em 2022, para 77% em 2023 e 88% em 2024. No ano passado, foi de 84,5%.

Os dados preliminares de 2026 apontam cobertura de 89,35% para a primeira dose e de 74,64% para a segunda. Embora os indicadores mostrem avanço em relação a 2022, a meta é alcançar cobertura de pelo menos 95% com as duas doses.

O CVE-SP confirmou 23 casos de sarampo no estado: 20 em moradores da capital, dois em São Bernardo do Campo e um em Guarulhos. Crianças menores de 2 anos foram o grupo mais atingido.

Nos três municípios, a vacinação foi ampliada para pessoas de 6 meses a 59 anos e segue até 1º de setembro. A dose é aplicada independentemente do histórico vacinal, após avaliação da equipe de saúde.

Crianças de 6 meses a 11 meses e 29 dias recebem a chamada dose zero. Essa dose é uma proteção adicional e não substitui as previstas no calendário: a primeira aos 12 meses e a segunda aos 15 meses, preferencialmente com a vacina tetraviral.

Além da vacinação, as ações do CVE-SP incluem investigação dos casos, monitoramento de contatos, busca ativa e orientação aos serviços de saúde. Todo caso suspeito deve ser notificado, isolado e investigado sem que seja necessário aguardar a confirmação laboratorial.

O sarampo pode provocar febre, manchas vermelhas pelo corpo, tosse, coriza e conjuntivite. Pessoas com esses sintomas devem procurar atendimento e informar se viajaram recentemente ou tiveram contato com alguém com quadro semelhante.

A Campanha de Multivacinação é voltada a crianças e adolescentes menores de 15 anos. Pais e responsáveis devem procurar uma unidade de saúde, preferencialmente com a caderneta de vacinação. A equipe confere o histórico e orienta sobre as doses indicadas para cada faixa etária.

As vacinas previstas no calendário são oferecidas gratuitamente pelo SUS. Os horários e os pontos de atendimento devem ser consultados junto ao município.

articles.title: Beauty therapist Chantelle Van Vliet was fired after asking for flexible hours over severe menopause symptoms, wins £32,237 in compensation after tribunal finds she was denied reasonable workplace support
articles.summary: UK News: For Chantelle Van Vliet, asking for a little flexibility at work became the beginning of a painful legal battle. The 48-year-old beauty therapist had .
articles.body: For Chantelle Van Vliet, asking for a little flexibility at work became the beginning of a painful legal battle. The 48-year-old beauty therapist had spent more than two decades building a career in the aesthetics industry, working at prestigious spas around the world and, apart from maternity leave, never experiencing a significant period of unemployment. But in 2024, severe menopause symptoms began affecting her daily life and her ability to work late shifts.When she asked her employer for a modest change to her working hours, she believed she was simply asking for support. Instead, she was dismissed days later when the clinic underwent a reorganisation.According to a report by The Independent, an employment tribunal has now awarded Van Vliet £32,237, finding that she had been subjected to disability discrimination.Her menopause symptoms became increasingly difficult to manageVan Vliet was employed as a Senior Aesthetic Therapist by Footlaffs Limited in Petersfield, Hampshire, from June 2022.From 2022 onwards, she experienced migraines, hot flushes and recurrent urinary tract infections. According to the tribunal, those symptoms became significantly worse during 2023 and early 2024.In April 2024, she spoke to clinic boss Karen Dodds about what she was experiencing and also discussed hormone replacement therapy.By May, her condition had become difficult enough that she had to take a day off because she "could not cope" with the severity of her symptoms.A week later, she made what appeared to be a straightforward request for workplace flexibility."I would like to ask for this request to get a better work and family balance," Van Vliet wrote in an email."I have also recently started going through the menopause which has really affected me, especially working the later shifts."She even suggested a three-month trial period, giving her employer an opportunity to see whether the arrangement worked.Her manager said the request would be discussed with Dodds. But, according to the tribunal, Van Vliet never received a further response.Days later, she was taken off the rotaAt the end of May, Van Vliet was informed that she had been removed from the following day's rota because she supposedly had no clients booked.The tribunal heard that this was not correct and that she did have clients scheduled.The following day, all Footlaffs employees were dismissed for redundancy.However, there was an important difference in what happened next.A large majority of the employees, including the other therapists working in aesthetics, were offered new contracts with a successor business operated by Karen and Stephen Dodds.Van Vliet was the only beauty therapist who was not rehired.No reason was given to her for why she had been left out.Tribunal finds she was put at a disadvantageVan Vliet subsequently took the business and Karen and Stephen Dodds to an employment tribunal in Southampton.Employment Judge Jonathan Burns found that there was little evidence to support an alternative explanation for why Van Vliet had not been selected to continue with the new business.The tribunal heard general claims about redundancy but found that there was no detailed evidence of financial, operational or other non-discriminatory reasons for excluding her.Judge Burns also found that Van Vliet's flexible working request was connected, at least in part, to her disability and that her employers had constructive knowledge of her condition.She had been placed at a "substantial disadvantage" because she struggled to work late shifts due to fatigue, confusion and brain fog."The flexible working request was in substance a request for a reasonable adjustment for disability," the judge concluded.He added that allowing her to change her shifts would have been a reasonable adjustment, describing the request as "modest and sensible".She was awarded £32,237Van Vliet won claims involving disability discrimination, wrongful dismissal, deduction of wages, failure to make reasonable adjustments and victimisation.The compensation included £3,228 for unpaid wages, £510 for notice pay, £12,077 for loss of salary and £16,422 for injury to feelings, bringing the final award to £32,237.The tribunal found that losing her job had a severe emotional impact on Van Vliet, affecting her confidence, causing distress and creating difficulties in her family life and everyday functioning.Claims of automatic unfair dismissal and direct discrimination, however, were dismissed.‘Companies shouldn't get away with how they treat people’The case has ended with a legal victory for Van Vliet, but there is another painful uncertainty: whether she will actually receive the money awarded to her.The new company, Always Time To Be Me Ltd, is in voluntary liquidation, leaving Van Vliet unsure about when she will be paid.She is now self-employed and runs her own beauty therapy business.Reflecting on the judgment, Van Vliet said she was angry about how she had been treated."They're absolutely awful people," she said."They're now just declaring bankruptcy so I don't know what's happening with payment. It's awful."But she hopes her case will have a wider impact, particularly for employees who may feel vulnerable discussing menopause symptoms at work."It's good to highlight this to other people and employers. Companies shouldn't get away with how they treat people," she added.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: What we know about deadly Nepal-Tibet floods
articles.summary: Hundreds are feared to have died in flooding and landslides on the border of Nepal and Tibet.
articles.body:
Massive landslides and flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border have caused widespread damage and left hundreds dead or missing.

Search and rescue operations are under way. Chinese state media has said there are significant casualties, while Nepalese officials anticipate "huge scale loss".

Nepal's foreign minister earlier said an earthquake was reported on the Tibet-Nepal border shortly before the landslide, suggesting it may have triggered the disaster.

But the United States Geological Survey's latest analysis suggests there was no earthquake, raising questions about what caused the landslide itself.

One possibility is that water from rainfall or melting ice may have destabilised the ground or ice, triggering a chain reaction.

Climate change is known to be driving faster glacier melt in the Hindu Kush Himalaya region, but scientists say it is too soon to pinpoint its role in this specific event.

Scientists are now trying to piece together the order of events.

They'll be looking at satellite images of exactly where the landslide occurred, whether any glacial lakes suddenly drained, and where the river might have become blocked, as well as data on recent rainfall.

A deluge of material careered towards northern Nepalese towns, including areas popular with mountaineering tourists and pilgrims. The border is around 40 miles (64.4km) north of Nepal's capital city Kathmandu.

Footage showed a wall of mud and rock sweeping away buildings, roads and vehicles, as people fled the fast-moving wave of material in the Nuwakot region.

Severe flooding have been reported along the Bhote Koshi, Trishuli and Narayani rivers.

Deaths have also been reported in villages on the Tibetan side of the border.

The number of people killed or missing is still becoming clear.

Nepal police have reported 157 bodies have been found, while China, which controls Tibet, says at least three people have died.

However, the eventual death toll is expected to be much higher.

According to Nepal's tourism board, 403 people are thought to be missing, including 341 foreign nationals, many from India.

Other foreign nationals from 26 countries are also thought to have been caught up in the landslide, including 47 people from the US and 33 from the UK.

Nepal's Prime Minister said "the entire nation has been left shocked and deeply distressed" and that officials would coordinate with China on the response.

China's President Xi Jinping urged an "all-out" search effort, and promised stronger monitoring and early warning systems to prevent secondary impacts.

In neighbouring India, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said his government was "prepared to provide Nepal with all possible types of humanitarian assistance".

UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the British government will do "everything we can" to support British nationals in Nepal.

articles.title: Videos show crushing walls of water overtake buildings and bridges on Nepal-Tibet border
articles.summary: Flash floods hit Himalayan mountain towns and villages, sweeping away vehicles, bridges and even buildings as people fled in terror.
articles.body: Crowds attempt to flee a surging wall of mud but have nowhere to go as it hits them with horrific force. Rows of buses and trucks parked nearby are swept aside like toys. Moments later, there is only wreckage and destruction. The shocking surveillance footage from the Rasuwagadhi border crossing, which links China’s semiautonomous Tibet region to Nepal, captures the scale of destruction as flash floods swept through Himalayan mountain towns and villages Wednesday, leaving ruins in their wake. In Nepal’s hardest-hit Rasuwa region, videos verified by NBC News showed bridges being cracked apart and swept away by the force of raging waters filled with mud and debris. Peaceful lush green valleys were transformed in an instant with the violence of churning water. Aboard a bus in Bidur, a passenger captures chaos as the surge appears in the distance: People scream and shout, some running away on foot, as vehicles on the road attempt to make their escape. Elsewhere, in videos shared by Nepali police, roads and buildings are swept away completely. Satellite imagery showed the scale of the flooding, with the basin of the Trishuli River dramatically swelled by mud. Hundreds of tourists are among the missing in the popular mountain regions north of Nepal’s capital, Kathmandu. At least 157 people have been killed, the country’s police service said. The true scale of the casualties may take days to become clear, however, with power and communication lines swept away in some areas. A State Department spokesperson said it “is aware of Americans impacted by the floods in Nepal and is closely tracking the situation.” High casualty counts are also feared in Tibet, where hundreds more are missing, with both Nepal and China declaring emergencies and scrambling rescue teams. “There is devastation everywhere we look,” Tula Bahadur BK, a health worker in Rasuwa, told Reuters. “The settlements next to the river have been completely swept away. Five of my own relatives are missing.” Sasmit Pokharel, a Nepali government spokesperson, said they have asked both India and China for help with the rescue efforts. The cause of the inundation was not immediately clear, but climate experts at the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development said an avalanche from a glacier likely caused Wednesday’s flash flood. The U.S. Geological Survey reported a magnitude-4.4 earthquake early Wednesday, about 60 miles north of Kathmandu. “The Lhende Khola has flooded twice in 14 months, this time triggered by an ice rock avalanche from a glacier on the Nepal side that blocked the river and released a sudden surge downstream,” said Saswata Sanyal, a disaster risk reduction specialist at the climate research group. He noted the importance of early warnings in “a warming Himalaya.” The Himalayan region, which spans several countries, including India, is especially vulnerable to heavy rains, floods and landslides because it is warming faster than the rest of the world due to human-caused climate change. Research shows that extreme weather events, including heat waves, rains and melting glaciers, have become more frequent. Researchers in Kathmandu found earlier this year that glaciers across the Hindu Kush Himalaya region are melting at an accelerating rate, with ice loss rates doubling since 2000, primarily due to rising global temperatures and climate change.

articles.summary: Bryan Kohberger won an evidentiary hearing in June 2027 after claiming his defense team convinced him to falsely confess to the Idaho murders.
articles.body: Convicted quadruple murderer Bryan Kohberger, who admitted to stabbing four University of Idaho students a year before he proclaimed his innocence and asked to withdraw his guilty plea, has been granted two days in court next year as part of his petition for post-conviction relief. Judge Steven Hippler, who accepted Kohberger's guilty pleas in July 2025, set a status conference for June 3, 2027, and an evidentiary hearing two weeks later on June 17 of that year, according to a court order dated Wednesday. Prosecutors had asked the judge to dismiss Kohberger's petition without a hearing. ATTORNEY WHO DEFENDED DC SNIPER SAYS KOHBERGER FACES 'MONUMENTAL UPHILL BATTLE' UNDOING GUILTY PLEA Kohberger pleaded guilty in July 2025 to the murders of four University of Idaho students — Madison Mogen, Kaylee Goncalves, Xana Kernodle and Ethan Chapin — in a plea deal that spared him from the potential death penalty. A year later, he asked to withdraw his guilty pleas and proclaimed his innocence in a petition for post-conviction relief. BRYAN KOHBERGER'S POST-CONVICTION RELIEF BID ENABLED BY FLAWED PLEA DEAL, PSYCHOLOGIST ARGUES Kohberger, in a handwritten petition on July 27, 2026, claimed that he was "convinced to falsely confess" by his high-profile defense team of Anne Taylor, Elisa Massoth and Bicka Barlow. He alleged that they failed to tell him about "exculpatory discovery" — hair found at the scene that was not tested for DNA. It was excluded as Kohberger's through a physical analysis. articles.title: In 1902, edible dormice were released at an English estate; by 2018 Britain had an estimated 23,000, and the government now pays £40 per hectare a year to control damage to trees, crops and nesting birds
articles.summary: UK News: In 1902, a small population of edible dormice was released at Tring Park, a private estate in Hertfordshire, as part of a Victorian-era fascination wi.
articles.body: In 1902, a small population of edible dormice was released at Tring Park, a private estate in Hertfordshire, as part of a Victorian-era fascination with exotic wildlife. More than a century later, that single introduction has grown into a national problem: by 2018, the Mammal Society estimated around 23,000 edible dormice lived in the UK, mostly in the Chiltern Hills. Today, the UK government pays land managers £40 per hectare per year under a Countryside Stewardship scheme to control these invasive rodents, which strip bark from trees, damage fruit crops and predate hole-nesting birds, according to official reports from GOV.UK. Read on to know more about it here:From estate curiosity to invasive speciesThe edible dormouse (Glis glis) is native to continental Europe and parts of Asia, not the British Isles. It was first introduced to the UK in 1902 at Tring Park in Hertfordshire, where it was kept in a semi-wild state on the estate. Over the following decades, some individuals escaped or were deliberately released, establishing a free-living population in nearby woodlands.Unlike many introduced species that fade away, edible dormice thrived. They are long-lived for a rodent, can breed successfully in woodland and orchard habitats, and have few natural predators in the UK. By 2018, their range had expanded to cover much of the Chiltern Hills and adjacent woodlands, with the population centred within about 35 km of Tring Park. The Mammal Society’s estimate of roughly 23,000 individuals marks the edible dormouse as one of Britain’s most successful invasive mammals.How edible dormice damage trees, crops and birdsEdible dormice are classified by the UK government as an invasive non-native species (INNS) because of the harm they cause to native habitats and species. Their most visible impact is on trees. In early summer, they strip bark from the crowns of pole-stage or mature trees, leaving distinctive rectangular patches. This can cause stem breakage, forking and, in severe cases, tree death. Preferred species include larch, Scots pine, Norway spruce, beech, birch and orchard trees.In orchards and other fruit-growing areas, dormice feed on fruit crops, reducing yields and quality. They also predate hole-nesting birds, taking eggs and chicks from nest boxes and natural cavities in trees. This combination of bark stripping, crop damage and predation makes them a significant problem for forestry, horticulture and wildlife conservation in the regions where they are established.Why the government pays land managers to control themBecause edible dormice are invasive and cause measurable economic and ecological harm, the UK government has created a dedicated funding stream to support their control. Under the Countryside Stewardship Higher Tier (CSHT) scheme, the “CSP20: Edible dormouse control and management” action pays land managers £40 per hectare per year for 10 years to reduce dormouse populations and limit damage.The aim of the action is clear: to control the population of invasive non-native edible dormice in order to reduce their impact on tree bark, fruit crops and hole-nesting birds, thereby supporting habitat and species recovery. Payments are made only where dormice are present and where land managers have an agreed species management plan with Natural England or the Forestry Commission. Participants must carry out baseline monitoring, agreed levels of culling, and habitat impact assessments in years 1, 5 and 10 of the agreement.How control is carried out—and the rules around itControl of edible dormice is tightly regulated to ensure it is humane, targeted and does not harm protected species. Management by trapping requires a specific wildlife licence (CL02) from Natural England. Trapping is typically carried out from May to August, when dormice are active and easier to catch.Land managers are advised to:Place traps in suitable habitat and minimise the risk of capturing non-target species.Bait traps for up to five days before setting them; if bait is taken, the trap can then be set.Check traps daily and release any non-target species as soon as possible.Maintain the health and welfare of any trapped animal and dispatch caught dormice humanely, usually by cranial concussion or an approved spring trap.Carcasses must be disposed of responsibly, for example by incineration or burial, with additional permissions required on sites of special scientific interest. All activities must comply with animal welfare legislation, including the Wild Mammals (Protection) Act 1996 and the Animal Welfare Act 2006.Not to be confused with the protected hazel dormouseA key challenge in managing edible dormice is avoiding harm to the native hazel dormouse (Muscardinus avellanarius), which is a protected species. The two look similar to non-specialists, but they differ in size, tail characteristics and habitat preferences. Government guidance stresses the importance of correct identification using non-native species secretariat (NNSS) ID sheets and, where necessary, advice from Natural England or Forestry Commission officers.Mistaking a hazel dormouse for an edible dormouse could lead to illegal killing of a protected species, so land managers are urged to be cautious and seek expert support if unsure.A long-term, landscape-scale problemThe edible dormouse story is a classic example of how a small, seemingly harmless introduction can become a long-term management issue. What began as an estate curiosity in 1902 has evolved into a landscape-scale problem requiring coordinated monitoring, licensing and funding.By paying land managers to control dormice in key areas, the government aims to limit further spread, reduce damage to trees and crops, and protect vulnerable wildlife such as hole-nesting birds. At the same time, the scheme reflects a broader shift in UK policy toward proactive management of invasive non-native species, recognising that prevention is far cheaper and more effective than trying to reverse established invasions.For now, the Chilterns remain the epicentre of the UK’s edible dormouse population, but occasional reports from other parts of the country serve as a reminder that vigilance is needed. Without continued control and monitoring, the legacy of that 1902 release could extend well beyond the woodlands of Hertfordshire and Buckinghamshire.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: For nearly a decade, a California town fought to seize its privately owned water utility; now the state Supreme Court has ruled 7-0 against its takeover argument
articles.summary: US News: California's highest court has rejected a key legal argument in a decade-long effort by a Southern California town to take control of its local water .
articles.body: California's highest court has rejected a key legal argument in a decade-long effort by a Southern California town to take control of its local water system. The California Supreme Court ruled 7-0, August 24, against the Town of Apple Valley, finding that judges do not have to automatically defer to local governments seeking to take private utilities through eminent domain. Writing for the unanimous court, Associate Justice Leondra Kruger rejected Apple Valley's argument that its declaration of public necessity should receive only limited judicial review. "The town of Apple Valley, which seeks to take over a privately owned water utility, argues that its decision to take the utility is subject to the usual standard governing judicial review of a resolution of necessity — meaning, in effect, that the court can disallow the taking only if it concludes that the town has committed a gross abuse of discretion," Kruger wrote in the court's opinion. "The Court of Appeal accepted this argument. We do not."Reporting by Courthouse News Service, republished by Maven's Notebook, said the ruling changes how courts review municipal attempts to take over private utilities in California. The decision could make it easier for private water, gas and electricity companies to challenge government seizures.Roots of a decade-long legal battleThe dispute in San Bernardino County began in 2010, when private equity firm Carlyle Infrastructure Partners bought the Apple Valley Ranchos Water Company, which served about 65,000 people. Large rate increases after the sale led to public anger and pushed town officials to consider taking over the system. In 2015, the Apple Valley Town Council approved formal resolutions of necessity to condemn the water system and take control of its infrastructure. During the early stages of the case, the utility was sold again to Liberty Utilities, a subsidiary of Canada-based Algonquin Power & Utilities Corp. Liberty Utilities strongly opposed the forced takeover in San Bernardino County Superior Court. The company argued that public ownership was neither necessary nor a better public use. After a 67-day bench trial, a Superior Court judge ruled for Liberty Utilities. The judge found that the company had successfully challenged the town's claims that the takeover was necessary. The trial court also ordered the town to pay Liberty Utilities 13.2 million dollars in legal fees. That ruling was later overturned by a state appeals court. The appeals court said judges must use a highly deferential "gross abuse of discretion" standard when reviewing local government resolutions of necessity.Setting limits on municipal powerThe Supreme Court's decision addresses the conflict between local governments' broad eminent domain powers and a 1992 California law that gives private utility companies additional protection. The court said the 1992 law was designed to provide stronger protection for privately owned utilities. Under the law, trial judges must independently examine the facts instead of simply accepting a local government's declaration. Kruger wrote that a municipal resolution cannot automatically approve a property seizure. "The resolution is not the be-all and end-all of a condemnation proceeding," Kruger wrote. "As a general rule, public necessity is a matter for the public entity to decide, subject to limited judicial review." However, the court said that when privately owned utility property is involved, judges must independently examine the evidence to determine whether the legal requirements for condemnation have actually been met. "To evaluate a challenge to the taking of privately owned public utility property, the trial court, sitting as trier of fact, must exercise its independent judgment to determine whether the utility owner challenging the taking has rebutted the relevant presumptions and has thus established by a preponderance of the evidence that the taking does not satisfy the statutory requirements," the ruling stated.Case sent back for reviewThe Supreme Court rejected Apple Valley's main legal argument but did not decide whether the town can ultimately take control of the water system. Instead, the unanimous ruling sends the case back to the California Court of Appeal for further proceedings under the new legal standard. The appeals court must reconsider the trial court's original findings. It will also examine separate procedural questions, including whether evidence collected after the 2015 resolutions were approved should have been allowed during the original trial. The ruling could affect other California communities pursuing similar utility takeovers. In San Francisco, city officials have spent years exploring the use of eminent domain to acquire Pacific Gas & Electric's local power grid and create a publicly owned electric utility. By requiring trial judges to independently examine the evidence rather than largely deferring to local officials, the California Supreme Court has raised the legal hurdle for municipalities seeking to take privately owned utility systems.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: Kai Cenat’s Streamer University was supposed to give aspiring creators a free shot at learning the game. Instead, the first sign-up rush became a problem of its own. When the website opened on May 6, 2025, it reportedly received more than 6 million web requests in hours. More than 1 million applications were completed before the platform froze, showing just how big the demand had become.The project itself was a Harry Potter-inspired, multi-day creator boot camp built around livestreaming and online content. Cenat rented the University of Akron in Ohio for the 2025 edition and brought together a group after the online application pool. The final class had only 120 student creators, with 17 professors involved. That gap shows how selective the program became.The free creator program became huge before classes even beganGetting in was the hard part. Those selected for Streamer University received an all-expenses-paid experience, including travel, food and housing. They also got sponsored T-Mobile phones. The training was focused on the actual work behind a creator career, with workshops covering livestream production, monetization, algorithmic optimization and audience retention.The faculty also came from the online creator world. Duke Dennis, Agent 00, DDG and ImDontai were among the names brought in as guest professors and mentors. So this was not just a classroom setup. The format was built around people already working inside the same internet-first space the students wanted to enter.Cenat refused to turn Streamer University into a normal TV showThe size of the event attracted attention from entertainment companies too. That choice also shaped how viewers experienced the event.The decision had a major payoff in terms of audience numbers. “Orientation Day” reached more than 10 million views, while viewers watched over 23 million hours of footage during the weekend. It had become a large-scale piece of livestream entertainment.The 2025 crash also changed how Kai Cenat’s Streamer University handled applicationsStreamer University later returned in 2026, but the application process looked very different. Cenat has also announced plans for future editions to move outside the United States, with the next session set for Europe.For the 2025 launch, though, the biggest story happened before the students even arrived. articles.title: In 2022, bird flu caused an entire Sandwich tern colony in England to be abandoned; four breeding seasons later, the birds have returned in record numbers, creating one of the country’s largest colonies
articles.summary: UK News: Four breeding seasons after a deadly bird flu outbreak forced a colony of Sandwich Terns to leave their nesting ground, the seabirds have returned in .
articles.body: Four breeding seasons after a deadly bird flu outbreak forced a colony of Sandwich Terns to leave their nesting ground, the seabirds have returned in record numbers, creating one of England's largest breeding sites. Monitoring reports published by Rare Bird Alert confirm that Sandwich Terns (Thalasseus sandvicensis) nested at RSPB Pagham Harbour in West Sussex in unprecedented numbers during the 2026 breeding season. The recovery comes four years after the highly infectious H5N1 strain of avian influenza badly affected seabird colonies across the UK. The outbreak killed large numbers of adults and chicks and forced surviving birds to leave long-established nesting areas. The return to Pagham Harbour is one of the most notable conservation recoveries along England's southern coast and an important sign of resilience for coastal wildlife.The damage caused by the 2022 outbreakUK seabird populations suffered major losses in 2022 when an unusually severe strain of avian flu spread through coastal nature reserves. Sandwich Terns were especially vulnerable because they breed in large, closely packed colonies on shingle banks and narrow island spits. During the breeding season, birds and their chicks live close together, allowing the virus to spread quickly. At the height of the 2022 outbreak, reserve wardens and conservationists recorded large numbers of dead adult terns and chicks at important sites across the UK. At Pagham Harbour, a nature reserve managed by the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB) near Chichester, the losses were so serious that the entire colony collapsed. The surviving adults abandoned their nests during the season, leaving the nesting spit empty for the rest of the year. At the time, it was unclear whether the birds would ever return in large enough numbers to rebuild the colony.Protecting the habitatThe return in 2026 followed several years of habitat work and predator protection carried out by RSPB staff, seasonal wardens and local volunteers. Conservation teams prepared the site for a possible return by creating safe and quiet areas for nesting. Shingle islands within the harbour were reshaped and cleared of growing vegetation, giving the birds better views of approaching predators. Wardens also installed electric fencing and anti-predator grids to protect nests from foxes and badgers. Seasonal patrols and water barriers helped reduce disturbance from people in boats and walkers near the nesting areas. According to field reports documented by Rare Bird Alert, these measures created suitable conditions when Sandwich Terns returned to West Sussex after spending the winter along the coast of West Africa.Record numbers and breeding successThe 2026 census showed that the Sandwich Tern colony at Pagham Harbour had grown well beyond its numbers before the bird flu outbreak, making the site an important stronghold for the species in Britain. RSPB wardens recorded hundreds of active nests across the protected shingle ridges. Large numbers of healthy chicks reaching the fledging stage also showed that the colony had a highly successful breeding season. The birds benefited from good supplies of sandeels and sprats in the coastal waters off West Sussex, providing an important food source for adults and chicks. The return of the Sandwich Terns has also helped other coastal birds. Smaller ground-nesting species, including Common Terns, Little Terns and Mediterranean Gulls, often build their nests around larger tern colonies. These birds benefit from the Sandwich Terns' aggressive group defence, which can help keep predatory gulls and crows away from nesting areas.Hope for UK seabirdsThe recovery at Pagham Harbour has offered new hope to scientists studying the long-term effects of bird flu on wild bird populations. A national assessment published in Bird Study by the British Trust for Ornithology (BTO), Natural England and NatureScot found that seabirds with long lifespans and low reproductive rates can take many years to recover after large-scale deaths. The return of a large Sandwich Tern colony within just four years shows that targeted local conservation work can help speed up recovery after a major wildlife disease outbreak. Conservationists remain alert to future changes or new strains of avian influenza. But the growing colony at Pagham Harbour provides a strong example of how wildlife can recover when natural habitats are protected and carefully managed.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: UK weather: New thunderstorm warnings as rain set to continue
articles.summary: The Met Office has issued fresh thunderstorm warnings for Thursday with the potential for England and Wales to see flash flooding as the unsettled weather continues.
articles.body:
The Met Office has issued fresh warnings for thunderstorms that will bring more wet weather to parts of the UK on Thursday.

The first warning is valid from 02:00 BST with thunder and heavy rain due to move across south-east England in the early hours of Thursday morning.

A second comes into force at 06:00 BST for a wider area of England and Wales. This will last through to 22:00 and may become slow moving in the afternoon and evening.

Downpours could bring localised flash flooding and travel disruption - with the wettest areas potentially seeing 75mm (3in) of rain. Large hail, lightning and gusty winds could accompany the showers and it will feel rather humid for many.

Spells of rain are set to continue over the weekend - a bank holiday for England, Wales and Northern Ireland - accompanied by windy conditions in the south.

Downpours drifting northwards on Thursday

Thursday morning will get off to a wet start in southern England and south Wales, with heavy downpours accompanied by lightning, hail and squally winds.

These will then move north across mid and north Wales, the Midlands and parts of eastern England, arriving in northern England during the early afternoon.

As this initial line of downpours clears northwards the skies will brighten and sunny spells will develop, but further scattered showers that could again be very heavy and thundery are possible.

Some rain is likely to arrive in Northern Ireland and Scotland later in the day, although these northern areas of the UK are likely to avoid the very wettest weather.

Why are there no thunderstorms showing on my app?

Within the Met Office yellow warning area, 20-30mm (0.8-1.2in) of rain could fall in just a few hours, with up to 50mm (2in) over a 12-hour period.

Hills exposed to the easterly wind could possibly see 75mm (3in).

Hazardous driving conditions are expected with a chance that roads will be closed and communities cut off.

Lightning strikes could lead to power cuts, and hailstones of 1-2cm (0.4-0.8in) are also possible.

The wet weather will be welcome news for the large areas of England and Wales that remain in drought , however there is the increased risk of flash flooding where the ground is very dry and hard.

Not enough rain will fall to alleviate the recent dry spell, with experts warning that months of persistent wet weather is needed to replenish water supplies.

The coming weekend brings a number of festivals and high-profile events.

Reading and Leeds Festivals both run from Thursday until Sunday, as does Creamfields in Cheshire.

Manchester Pride takes place from Friday until Bank Holiday Monday, while Saturday marks the start of Notting Hill Carnival in London, which also continues until Monday.

The weather looks decidedly mixed for these events, with a fresher feel, brisk winds - especially in the south - and the likelihood of rain at times.

A zone of wet weather will move eastwards across England and Wales on Saturday, although drier and brighter conditions may spread from the west later. Northern Ireland and Scotland will be a little drier with some sunny spells, but there is still the chance of a few showers.

More heavy showers will move eastwards on Sunday, this time affecting most parts of the UK. Some of these could be heavy and thundery, with wind gusts touching 40-45mph (64-72km/h) in the far south-west of England later.

Temperatures will tend to range from 16C (61F) in northern Scotland to 23C (73F) in southern England, which is about normal for late August.

Low pressure remains in charge on Monday meaning strong winds and further showers, perhaps heaviest across the north of the UK.

There is no sign of a return to the dry and hot weather that has dominated this summer.

Whatever your plans for the weekend, you can keep up to date with the forecast by checking the BBC Weather website and app .

articles.title: Police: At least 157 dead after flash flood in Nepal
articles.summary: The death toll from severe flash floods in a mountainous region of Nepal has risen to at least 157, police said. Hundreds of people remain unaccounted for fo...
articles.body:
The death toll from severe flash floods in a mountainous region of Nepal has risen to at least 157, police said.

Hundreds of people remain unaccounted for following the disaster, which caused widespread destruction along the Bhotekoshi River near the border with China.

Those reported missing include hundreds of foreign tourists as well as Nepalese travellers and members of the police and security forces.

Homes, roads, bridges and hydropower facilities were destroyed as the water surged mountain valleys, with Nepal's Rasuwa district particularly badly affected.

So far, neighbouring China has reported three deaths and 265 people missing in south-western Tibet.

What triggered the flash floods on Wednesday morning remains unclear. One hypothesis being considered by authorities is the outburst of a glacial lake in Tibet, in which a lake fed by melting glaciers suddenly releases a massive volume of water.

articles.title: Judge clears path for ICE agent accused in Minnesota shooting case to leave Texas jail
articles.summary: A federal judge denied Minnesota's temporary restraining order, potentially clearing ICE agent Christian Castro's release from Cameron County Jail.
articles.body: A federal judge on Wednesday handed Minnesota a major setback in its fight to keep ICE agent Christian Castro behind bars in Texas, denying an emergency request that would have blocked his release Thursday. U.S. District Judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr. rejected Minnesota’s request for a temporary restraining order barring Cameron County Sheriff Manuel Trevino from releasing Castro while Texas Gov. Greg Abbott decides whether to extradite the agent to face assault charges. Castro’s 90-day detention period under Texas law expires Thursday. Trevino’s counsel told the court that without a court order or a rendition warrant signed by Abbott, Castro would be released from the Cameron County Jail. Rodriguez wrote that Minnesota "fails to satisfy the requirements for the issuance of a temporary restraining order." 'POLITICAL STUNT' PROSECUTION OF ICE AGENT FOR 'ROAD RAGE' PROVOKES HEATED DHS RESPONSE Minnesota had asked the court to force Abbott to immediately issue a rendition warrant and prevent Castro’s release in the meantime. The state warned Castro could flee to Mexico, pointing to jail calls with a woman described in court filings as his romantic partner who lives in Progreso, Mexico. According to the order, Castro discussed buying property and moving to Mexico in the future. Minnesota argued that if he left the country, it could take months or years to secure his return and prosecute him. But Rodriguez ruled that Minnesota’s lawsuit was premature because Abbott has not yet denied its extradition request. "The record reflects only that Governor Abbott has neither agreed nor refused to sign the rendition warrant as to Castro," the judge wrote. Abbott instead directed the Texas secretary of state to investigate whether Castro should be surrendered, a step permitted under Texas’ Uniform Criminal Extradition Act. Rodriguez found that neither the Constitution nor state and federal extradition laws at issue impose a set deadline for Abbott to complete that review. "The Court concludes that this matter does not present an issue ripe for adjudication," Rodriguez wrote. Minnesota formally requested Castro’s extradition in early June, after he was arrested in Cameron County on the state’s warrant. The court noted Abbott has considered the matter for an "atypically-long duration," but said Minnesota identified no law requiring the governor to act within a particular time frame. TIM WALZ PARDONS ILLEGAL ALIEN CONVICTED OF ARMED ROBBERY BEFORE ICE DEPORTATION TO LAOS Castro was charged in May with four felony counts of second-degree assault and one misdemeanor count of falsely reporting a crime stemming from a January ICE operation in Minnesota. According to the order, Castro fired one shot through the closed front door of a home, injuring a person in the leg. The shooting sparked protests in north Minneapolis and has become part of a broader political and legal battle between Minnesota officials and the Trump administration over state prosecutions of ICE agents who took part in Operation Metro Surge. 15 ANTIFA RADICALS INDICTED, 12 ARRESTED IN SWEEPING FEDERAL PROBE INTO MINNEAPOLIS ANTI-ICE OPERATIONS Minnesota prosecutors have separately charged ICE agent Gregory Morgan Jr. with two counts of second-degree assault after alleging he pointed a handgun at motorists during a traffic confrontation after an enforcement operation. DHS has accused Minnesota "sanctuary politicians" of staging a "political stunt," while Minnesota officials have argued the agents’ alleged conduct fell outside their federal law-enforcement duties. Abbott has raised questions about whether Castro can be considered a fugitive for extradition purposes because he returned to Texas on orders from federal immigration officials after the January incident. Rodriguez, however, signaled skepticism of that reasoning in a footnote. "The Court has doubts that caselaw supports the construction of ‘fugitive’ that Texas is considering," he wrote, noting that longstanding precedent appears to focus on whether an accused person left the state — not why. Still, the judge said that question did not alter Wednesday’s decision. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The ruling leaves Castro’s immediate fate in Abbott’s hands. If no rendition warrant is issued and no court order intervenes, he is expected to be released Thursday. Abbott and Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's requests for comment. Fox News' Patrick McGovern and Elaine Mallon contributed to this report.
